chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) used to say: 'If I were to bequeath a fifth of my wealth, it would be more beloved to me than bequeathing a quarter; and if I were to bequeath a quarter, it would be more beloved to me than bequeathing a third; and whoever bequeaths a third and leaves nothing back, he has gone to the extreme.'

He said: And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who died and bequeathed all or most of his wealth, saying: 'The bequest is to be returned to what is acceptable and away from what is reprehensible. So whoever wrongs himself and commits the reprehensible and injustice in his bequest, it shall be returned to what is acceptable, and the share of the inheritance shall be left for the heirs.'

And he said: 'Whoever bequeaths a third of his wealth and leaves nothing back, he has reached the (upper) limit.' Then he said: 'If I were to bequeath a fifth of my wealth, it would be more beloved to me than bequeathing a quarter.'

key_terms.أهل الميراث: The people of inheritance — the legal heirs entitled to their prescribed shares
key_terms.الحيف: Injustice/unfairness — deliberate harm done to heirs through an excessive bequest
key_terms.المعروف: The acceptable/recognized good — the established limit of one-third for bequests in Islamic law
key_terms.المنكر: The reprehensible/unacceptable — exceeding the permitted third in bequest
key_terms.الوصية: Bequest/testament — a legal declaration disposing of one's property upon death, capped at one-third according to Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the recommended amount for a bequest (wasiyya) in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) quotes Imam Ali (AS) expressing a strong preference for smaller bequests — preferring one-fifth over one-quarter, and one-quarter over one-third — indicating that bequeathing the full third is reaching the maximum permissible limit. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential stance, rooted in Quranic guidance (2:180, 4:11), that heirs have primary rights to the estate and that a testator should not deprive them by excessive bequests. Imam Ali's judicial ruling further clarifies that any bequest exceeding the norm of good practice must be reduced to protect the heirs' shares.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aasim Bin Hameed, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> says that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘If I<sup>asws</sup> were to bequeath with a fifth of my<sup>asws</sup> wealth, it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than if I<sup>asws</sup> were to bequeath with a quarter of it; and if I<sup>asws</sup> were to bequeath with a quarter, it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than if I<sup>asws</sup> were to bequeath with a third; and if one were to bequeath with a third, so he has not left out anything, so he has reached (the upper limit)’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged with regards to a man who died and bequeathed with his wealth, all of it or most of it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The bequest is to be returned to from unacceptable level to what is acceptable, other than what will harm (heir) (undefined). So the one who is unjust to himself, and made a will which is harmful and the injustice, so it should be returned to the specified once (one fifth), and there should be left for the people of the inheritance, their inheritances’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who bequeaths with a third of his wealth, so he does not leave out anything, so he has reached the (upper) limit’. 
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If I<sup>asws</sup> were to bequeath with a fifth of my<sup>asws</sup> wealth, it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than if I<sup>asws</sup> were to bequeath with the fourth’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in this statement refers to the words of ’Amir al-Mu’minin. He (the Imam) said, ‘If I make a will about one-fifth of my legacy it is better than making a will about one- fourth of my legacy, and if I make a will about one-fourth of my legacy it is better than a will about one-third of my legacy. One who makes a will about one-third of his legacy and leaves nothing, he has exaggerated.’

“He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin issued a judgment in the case of a man who had made a will about all of his legacy or most of it. He (the Imam) said, ‘The will is turned from unacceptable status into what is acceptable. If one does injustice to himself and comes up with an unacceptable will and an unjust one, it then is turned to an acceptable one to leave the legacy for the heirs.’

’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘If one makes a will about one-third of his legacy which does not leave anything for the heirs, he has reached the ultimate condition.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘If one makes a will about one-fifth of his legacy it is more likable to me than a will about one-fourth.’”
